title: Addressing Pitfalls in Auditing Practices of Automatic Speech Recognition Technologies: A Case Study of People with Aphasia

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing Word Error Rate (WER), hallucination rates, and a suite of NLP metrics (e.g., BLEU, ROUGE, Word Information Lost) between speakers with aphasia and a control group without speech disorders using the AphasiaBank dataset. The analysis also disaggregates performance by aphasia severity and subtype (e.g., fluent vs. non-fluent, Broca's, Global).
Evaluating and comparing ASR performance (WER) and hallucination rates across gender subgroups (male vs. female), both as an independent variable and intersectionally with aphasia severity.
Analyzing ASR performance disparities across racial demographics (specifically comparing African American and White speakers) using regression models and subgroup analysis.
Including age and age-squared as covariates in linear and probit regression models to measure the effect of a speaker's age on ASR transcription error rates and hallucination likelihood.
Using educational attainment levels (e.g., less than 4-year college, 4-year college, post-grad degree) as demographic covariates in regression analyses to predict ASR performance disparities.
